set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit. The usual way down is the Kraus-McCarthy rappel line on the west face, on bolted and chained anchors. Afterward walk north to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and rappel or downclimb its snow, or head south to the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels, which end on the Bugaboo Glacier and are a longer way back. Rope up for the crevasses on either glacier. The col is quicker but has been affected by rockfall and melt, so check current conditions. Reversing the original Wiessner chimney line is the older alternative.
set.approach: Start at the end of the park road at the Bugaboo Creek trailhead and take the Conrad Kain Hut trail, about 5 km one way with roughly 700 m of gain, steep and with chained sections near the top. From the hut area continue up onto the Pigeon arm of the Bugaboo Glacier. Pass the steep rock of the southeast spur, then cross snow to a col in the spur, where the roped climbing begins. Rope up for crevasses and carry an axe and crampons.

review.notes: Descent options and summit top-out from the route page; rappel line and col from the West Face page. Counts omitted (one lineage). Trail 5 km/700 m from three pages.

set.descent_text: The route reaches the south summit by scrambling or simul-climbing above the top of the wall. Descend by the Kraus-McCarthy rappels, which have chain anchors; some rappels are tight for a single rope, so knot the ends, and the second one is known to eat ropes. From the bottom, use the col, or the longer rappels on the Pigeon side.
set.approach: Start at the end of the park road at the Bugaboo Creek trailhead and take the Conrad Kain Hut trail, about 5 km one way with roughly 700 m of gain, steep and with chained sections near the top. Climbers camp at the hut or at the Applebee Dome campground on the rock slab above it. Surfs Up is at the south end of the west face, just left of the Pigeon icefall rappel line. The west face is reached by crossing the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col; rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base. From the col a snow slope leads along the foot of the face to the start. Check current park notices for rockfall closures on the spire before committing.

review.notes: Both route pages put the start via the col and the descent on Kraus-McCarthy. Counts omitted.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit ridge. From the rappel bolts a short third-class scramble reaches the true summit. Descend by the Kraus-McCarthy rappels on bolted and chained anchors, then choose the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col, which is much faster back to Applebee, or the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels. If the final slabs hold snow, a tricky variation west of the wet area avoids them. Swap wet rock shoes for approach shoes at the bottom if snow remains.
set.approach: Start at the end of the park road at the Bugaboo Creek trailhead and take the Conrad Kain Hut trail, about 5 km one way with roughly 700 m of gain, steep and with chained sections near the top. Climbers camp at the hut or at the Applebee Dome campground on the rock slab above it. The route shares its first pitches with Surfs Up on the south end of the west face. The face is reached by crossing the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col; rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base. From the col a snow slope leads along the foot of the face to the start. Check current park notices for rockfall closures on the spire before committing.

review.notes: Top-out and descent from the route page, checked against Surfs Up. Counts omitted.

set.descent_text: Scramble south from the summit ridge to the bolt anchors on the west face and descend the bolted rappel line from there, the same west-face line the common Kraus-McCarthy descent uses. At the bottom continue to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col or the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels.
set.approach: Start at the end of the park road at the Bugaboo Creek trailhead and take the Conrad Kain Hut trail, about 5 km one way with roughly 700 m of gain, steep and with chained sections near the top. Climbers camp at the hut or at the Applebee Dome campground on the rock slab above it. Wildflowers follows a large left-facing dihedral almost directly below the south summit, starting from a ledge about 200 feet below the dihedral. The west face is reached by crossing the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col; rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base. From the col a snow slope leads along the foot of the face to the start. Check current park notices for rockfall closures on the spire before committing.

review.notes: Own page for top-out and start; West Face page for the rappel line.

set.descent_text: The route tops out beside the Kraus-McCarthy rappel line, so the rappel stations are right there. Rappel that line on its bolted and chained anchors and finish via the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col or the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels.
set.approach: Start at the end of the park road at the Bugaboo Creek trailhead and take the Conrad Kain Hut trail, about 5 km one way with roughly 700 m of gain, steep and with chained sections near the top. Climbers camp at the hut or at the Applebee Dome campground on the rock slab above it. The route lies just south of the Kraus-McCarthy rappel line on the west face, which makes it a short outing from the col. The west face is reached by crossing the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col; rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base. From the col a snow slope leads along the foot of the face to the start. Check current park notices for rockfall closures on the spire before committing.

review.notes: Location line plus West Face page.

set.descent_text: This version stops on top of a tower and does not continue to the summit. Rappel the route with two ropes from the fixed anchors; the anchors vary in condition, so carry gear or webbing to back them up, and watch for rope-eating flakes. The line is cold and loose, so keep ropes clear of loose rock on the way down.
set.approach: Start at the end of the park road at the Bugaboo Creek trailhead and take the Conrad Kain Hut trail, about 5 km one way with roughly 700 m of gain, steep and with chained sections near the top. Climbers camp at the hut or at the Applebee Dome campground on the rock slab above it. The route is on the northernmost part of the west face and faces northwest, so it stays cold. Cross the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col; rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base. The climbing starts at the top of the col, with a first stretch of about 70 m. Check current park notices for rockfall closures on the spire before committing.

review.notes: Single route page for the start at the col and the rappel descent; anchors there are dated, hence the warning.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route itself on its anchors, which are mostly slung webbing and fixed nuts or pins, so bring extra webbing. Plan on two ropes. Expect to be in shade and cold for most of the descent.
set.approach: Start at the end of the park road at the Bugaboo Creek trailhead and take the Conrad Kain Hut trail, about 5 km one way with roughly 700 m of gain, steep and with chained sections near the top. Climbers camp at the hut or at the Applebee Dome campground on the rock slab above it. This one lies on the north side of the spire. Climb the slope toward the col, then cut left at about mid-height onto a ledge strewn with loose rock. Begin beneath the conspicuous wide crack, to the right of a big blocky corner. Carry an axe and crampons, and rope up for the glacier.

review.notes: Single route page: location line gives the traverse and rappel-the-route descent.

set.descent_text: This is the line most parties use to rappel from the summit area. Bolt-and-chain anchors run down the face, and some single rappels barely reach, so knot the rope ends. At the bottom continue to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col or the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels.

review.notes: West Face page describes the rappel line; no approach given for this row specifically, so approach omitted.

set.approach: Start at the end of the park road at the Bugaboo Creek trailhead and take the Conrad Kain Hut trail, about 5 km one way with roughly 700 m of gain, steep and with chained sections near the top. Climbers camp at the hut or at the Applebee Dome campground on the rock slab above it. The route climbs the east face: locate the obvious scoop in the large rock scar and start off the snow in the cracks on the left side of it. descend to the glacier below the wall and walk to the base, stepping across the moat at the rock, which gets harder as summer goes on. Bring an axe and rope for the glacier.
